name: Ishi
overview: Ishi was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the father of Zoheth and the grandfather (or possibly father) of Ben-zoheth. His mention in Scripture highlights his role within the genealogical records of Judah. Beyond his lineage, there are no additional notes or details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishi means 'G-d has saved,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew name though it was not given directly by God. This name emphasizes divine salvation, a theme consistent with the faith of the patriarchal tribes.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ishi as the father of Zoheth and the father or grandfather of Ben-zoheth. Additional inferred relationships include his fatherhood of Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, indicating his role as a progenitor within his family line as documented in 1 Chronicles 4:20 and 4:42.
scriptureSignificance: Ishi's significance lies chiefly in his place within the genealogical framework of Judah, serving as a link in the lineage that preserves the heritage of the tribe. His descendants, including Zoheth and Ben-zoheth, are noted in the chronicler's records, underscoring the importance of family lines in God's providential plan. While not prominent in narrative events, Ishi's mention contributes to the biblical emphasis on heritage and God's faithfulness through generations.
